entities.summary: Louis Pierre de Chastenet, comte de Puységur was a French soldier under the Ancien Régime. A lieutenant général from 1781, he became minister of war in the ministry of Jacques Necker, from 30 November 1788 to 12 July 1789. Replaced by Victor-François, 2nd duc de Broglie, he received marks of esteem from the Assembly. Remaining faithful to the king, he commanded a small troop of gentlemen and defended the Tuileries against the Revolutionaries on 10 August 1792, and emigrated soon afterwards. He returned on Napoleon's seizure of power on 18 Brumaire and institution of the First French Empire, and died in his home town.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As minister of war from November 1788 to July 1792, Louis Pierre de Chastenet de Puységur played a role in the lead-up to the French Revolution. He remained loyal to King Louis XVI and defended the Tuileries against revolutionaries on August 10, 1792.
